title: Arrival of the General
statementMd:
A Ministry for Defense sent a general to inspect the Super Secret Military Squad under the command of the Colonel SuperDuper. Having learned the news, the colonel ordered to all $*n*$ squad soldiers to line up on the parade ground.

By the military charter the soldiers should stand in the order of non-increasing of their height. But as there's virtually no time to do that, the soldiers lined up in the arbitrary order. However, the general is rather short-sighted and he thinks that the soldiers lined up correctly if the first soldier in the line has the maximum height and the last soldier has the minimum height. Please note that the way other solders are positioned does not matter, including the case when there are several soldiers whose height is maximum or minimum. Only the heights of the **first** and the **last** soldier are important.

For example, the general considers the sequence of heights `(4, 3, 4, 2, 1, 1)` correct and the sequence `(4, 3, 1, 2, 2)` wrong.

Within one second the colonel can swap any two neighboring soldiers. Help him count the minimum time needed to form a line-up which the general will consider correct.

## Input

The first input line contains the only integer $*n*$ ($2 ≤ *n* ≤ 100$) which represents the number of soldiers in the line. The second line contains integers $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ ($1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 100$) the values of the soldiers' heights in the order of soldiers' heights' increasing in the order from the beginning of the line to its end. The numbers are space-separated. Numbers $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ are not necessarily different.

## Output

Print the only integer — the minimum number of seconds the colonel will need to form a line-up the general will like.

## Note

In the first sample the colonel will need to swap the first and second soldier and then the third and fourth soldier. That will take 2 seconds. The resulting position of the soldiers is `(44, 33, 22, 11)`.

In the second sample the colonel may swap the soldiers in the following sequence:

1. `(10, 10, 58, 31, 63, 40, 76)`
2. `(10, 58, 10, 31, 63, 40, 76)`
3. `(10, 58, 10, 31, 63, 76, 40)`
4. `(10, 58, 10, 31, 76, 63, 40)`
5. `(10, 58, 31, 10, 76, 63, 40)`
6. `(10, 58, 31, 76, 10, 63, 40)`
7. `(10, 58, 31, 76, 63, 10, 40)`
8. `(10, 58, 76, 31, 63, 10, 40)`
9. `(10, 76, 58, 31, 63, 10, 40)`
10. `(76, 10, 58, 31, 63, 10, 40)`
11. `(76, 10, 58, 31, 63, 40, 10)`
statementZhMd:
国防部派遣一名将军，前往检阅由 SuperDuper 上校指挥的超级秘密军事小队。得知这一消息后，上校命令全部 $*n*$ 名士兵在阅兵场列队。

根据军队条例，士兵应按身高不递增的顺序站立。但由于几乎没有时间这样做，士兵们只能按任意顺序列队。然而，将军视力不佳，他认为只要队伍中的第一名士兵身高最高，最后一名士兵身高最低，列队就是正确的。请注意，其他士兵的位置无关紧要，包括有多名士兵身高并列最高或并列最低的情况。只有**第一名**和**最后一名**士兵的身高重要。

例如，将军认为身高序列 `(4, 3, 4, 2, 1, 1)` 是正确的，而序列 `(4, 3, 1, 2, 2)` 是错误的。

上校每秒可以交换任意两名相邻的士兵。请帮助他计算出形成一列将军认为正确的队伍所需的最短时间。

## 输入格式

第一行包含唯一的整数 $*n*$（$2 ≤ *n* ≤ 100$），表示队伍中士兵的数量。第二行包含整数 $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 100$），表示从队伍开头到末尾排列的士兵身高。数字之间用空格分隔。数字 $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ 不一定互不相同。

## 输出格式

输出唯一的整数——上校将队伍整理成将军满意的样子所需的最少秒数。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，上校需要先交换第一名和第二名士兵，然后交换第三名和第四名士兵。这将耗时 2 秒。交换后的士兵位置为 `(44, 33, 22, 11)`。

在第二个样例中，上校可以按如下顺序交换士兵：

1. `(10, 10, 58, 31, 63, 40, 76)`
2. `(10, 58, 10, 31, 63, 40, 76)`
3. `(10, 58, 10, 31, 63, 76, 40)`
4. `(10, 58, 10, 31, 76, 63, 40)`
5. `(10, 58, 31, 10, 76, 63, 40)`
6. `(10, 58, 31, 76, 10, 63, 40)`
7. `(10, 58, 31, 76, 63, 10, 40)`
8. `(10, 58, 76, 31, 63, 10, 40)`
9. `(10, 76, 58, 31, 63, 10, 40)`
10. `(76, 10, 58, 31, 63, 10, 40)`
11. `(76, 10, 58, 31, 63, 40, 10)`
